Title: Choosing How to Remember: Adaptive Memory Structures for LLM Agents
Abstract/Description: Proposes FluxMem, a framework for adaptive memory organization in AI agents. Addresses one-size-fits-all memory structure limitations by enabling context-adaptive memory structure selection with a three-level memory hierarchy and probabilistic fusion. Achieved 9.18% and 6.14% improvements on two benchmarks.
Key Insight: Context-adaptive memory selection is critical — different tasks need different memory structures, directly relevant to our specialisation goal

Title: HyMem: Hybrid Memory Architecture with Dynamic Retrieval Scheduling
Authors/Maintainers: Xiaochen Zhao, Kaikai Wang, Xiaowen Zhang, Chen Yao, Aili Wang
Abstract/Description: Proposes a hybrid memory architecture with multi-granular memory representations. Uses dual-granular storage scheme with dynamic two-tier retrieval system. Reduces computational cost by 92.6% while outperforming full-context approaches on LOCOMO and LongMemEval benchmarks.
Key Insight: Dual-granular storage (summary + detail) with dynamic retrieval scheduling — applicable to our tiered memory approach

Title: The Pensieve Paradigm: Stateful Language Models Mastering Their Own Context
Abstract/Description: Introduces StateLM with internal reasoning loop for context management. Equips models with memory tools like context pruning, document indexing, and note-taking. Achieved 10-20% accuracy improvement on chat memory tasks and up to 52% on deep research vs 5% for standard LLMs.
Key Insight: Self-managing memory tools (pruning, indexing, note-taking) can be given to agents as tools rather than building separate memory infrastructure

Title: ProcMEM: Learning Reusable Procedural Memory from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents
Authors/Maintainers: Qirui Mi, Zhijian Ma, Mengyue Yang, Haoxuan Li, Yisen Wang, Haifeng Zhang, Jun Wang
Abstract/Description: Framework enabling agents to autonomously learn procedural memory from interaction experiences. Transforms passive episodic narratives into executable Skills defined by activation, execution, and termination conditions. Uses Non-Parametric PPO for skill generation without parameter updates.
Key Insight: Transforming episodic experience into reusable procedural skills is exactly what we need for turning error/fix learnings into step-by-step procedures

Title: MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents
Abstract/Description: Modular multi-agent memory system with six memory types: Core, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Resource, and Knowledge Vault. Achieved 35% higher accuracy on benchmarks with 99.9% reduced storage. Supports multimodal memory.
Key Insight: Six-type memory taxonomy (Core/Episodic/Semantic/Procedural/Resource/Vault) provides comprehensive architecture blueprint for our system

Title: CAST: Character-and-Scene Episodic Memory for Agents
Authors/Maintainers: Kexin Ma, Bojun Li, Yuhua Tang, Liting Sun, Ruochun Jin
Abstract/Description: Proposes episodic memory architecture inspired by dramatic theory. Constructs 3D scenes (time/place/topic) and character profiles. Combines episodic with graph-based semantic memory. Improved by 8.11% F1 and 10.21% judge score for open and time-sensitive questions.
Key Insight: Scene-based episodic memory (time/place/topic) maps well to our deployment episodes (timestamp/environment/issue-type)

Title: TraceMem: Weaving Narrative Memory Schemata from User Conversational Traces
Authors/Maintainers: Yiming Shu, Pei Liu, Tiange Zhang, Ruiyang Gao, Jun Ma, Chen Sun
Abstract/Description: Three-stage brain-inspired memory processing: Short-term Memory Processing, Synaptic Memory Consolidation, Systems Memory Consolidation. Creates structured narrative memory schemata. State-of-the-art on LoCoMo benchmark.
Key Insight: Three-stage consolidation pipeline (short-term → synaptic → systems) provides a template for our memory consolidation architecture

Title: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
Abstract/Description: Memory-based online reinforcement learning for agent adaptation without fine-tuning. Uses Memory-augmented MDP with neural case-selection policy. Achieved 87.88% Pass@3 on GAIA. Stores past experiences in episodic memory with rewriting for policy improvement.
Key Insight: Memory-based RL without fine-tuning — agents improve by better selecting from past experiences, applicable to our feedback loop design

Title: Collaborative Memory: Multi-User Memory Sharing in LLM Agents with Dynamic Access Control
Authors/Maintainers: Alireza Rezazadeh, Zichao Li, Ange Lou, Yuying Zhao, Wei Wei, Yujia Bao
Abstract/Description: Framework for multi-user multi-agent memory sharing with private and shared tiers. Uses bipartite graphs for asymmetric dynamic access controls. Enables safe and interpretable cross-user knowledge sharing.
Key Insight: Private + shared memory tiers with access control maps to our per-agent specialisation memory + shared knowledge pool

Title: Enhancing MCP with Context-Aware Server Collaboration
Abstract/Description: Proposes Context-Aware MCP (CA-MCP) with Shared Context Store (SCS) for autonomous server coordination. Reduces LLM calls and improves reliability in multi-agent workflows on TravelPlanner and REALM-Bench.
Key Insight: MCP-based shared context store could be used for cross-agent memory sharing in our GitHub Actions pipeline

Title: Evolving Programmatic Skill Networks
Authors/Maintainers: Haochen Shi, Xingdi Yuan, Bang Liu
Abstract/Description: Framework for continual skill acquisition using symbolic programs and LLMs. Skills form compositional networks that evolve through experience. Features REFLECT for fault analysis and maturity-aware update gating.
Key Insight: Maturity-aware skill update gating — skills are refined through experience, similar to how our agent procedures should mature

Title: CogEvo-Edu: Cognitive Evolution Educational Multi-Agent Collaborative System
Authors/Maintainers: Yefeng Wu, Yuchen Song, Yecheng Zhao, Ling Wu, Shan Wan
Abstract/Description: Hierarchical multi-agent system with Cognitive Perception, Knowledge Evolution, and Meta-Control layers. Uses confidence-weighted consolidation and spatiotemporal value for knowledge management.
Key Insight: Confidence-weighted consolidation with spatiotemporal value scoring — applicable to ranking our learnings by confidence and recency

Title: SAMEP: Secure Protocol for Persistent Context Sharing Across AI Agents
Abstract/Description: Distributed memory repository with vector-based semantic search for persistent context sharing across AI agents. Focuses on security of shared memory.
Key Insight: Security considerations for shared agent memory — relevant as our agents run in GitHub Actions with AWS credentials

Title: RCR-Router: Efficient Role-Aware Context Routing for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Abstract/Description: Dynamic selection of semantically relevant memory subsets based on agent role. Efficient context routing for multi-agent systems.
Key Insight: Role-aware memory routing directly addresses our specialisation requirement — DevOps agent gets DevOps-relevant memories

Title: Letta (MemGPT)
Abstract/Description: Platform for building stateful agents with self-editing memory. Tiered memory: core (in-context), archival (long-term vector store), recall (conversation history). PostgreSQL backend with pgvector. Supports memory blocks with configurable labels. TypeScript SDK available: @letta-ai/letta-client.
Key Insight: Self-editing memory and tiered architecture (core/archival/recall) is the most mature agent memory framework. TypeScript SDK available but requires running Letta server.

Title: Mem0
Abstract/Description: Universal memory layer for AI agents. Multi-level memory (User, Session, Agent state). Graph-based memory with vector search. 26% accuracy improvement over OpenAI Memory, 91% faster responses, 90% lower token usage. Both Python and TypeScript SDKs (mem0ai npm package). Apache 2.0 license.
Key Insight: Most production-ready memory-as-a-service with TypeScript SDK. Graph + vector hybrid retrieval. Direct npm install makes integration easiest for our TypeScript agent.

Title: Zep
Abstract/Description: End-to-end context engineering platform. Temporal knowledge graph for context evolution. Sub-200ms retrieval latency. Extracts relationships and facts automatically. Python, TypeScript (@getzep/zep-cloud), and Go SDKs. Community Edition deprecated; focus on Zep Cloud (commercial).
Key Insight: Temporal knowledge graph is powerful for tracking how learnings evolve over time. However CE deprecated means cloud-only which adds vendor dependency.

Title: CrewAI
Abstract/Description: Multi-agent framework with unified memory system. Hierarchical scope tree, composite scoring (semantic similarity + recency + importance). Supports shallow (vector) and deep (LLM-based) recall. Background processing for non-blocking saves. Python only, no TypeScript SDK.
Key Insight: Unified memory with composite scoring (similarity + recency + importance) and hierarchical scopes is an excellent architectural pattern to adopt.

Title: Microsoft AutoGen
Abstract/Description: Multi-agent AI framework with layered API (Core, AgentChat, Extensions). Supports agent memory through teachability pattern. Cross-language support (.NET and Python). 54.6k stars. No native TypeScript SDK but .NET interop possible.
Key Insight: Teachability agent pattern (agents that learn from corrections) is relevant but Python-only and heavy framework dependency.

Title: Microsoft Semantic Kernel
Abstract/Description: SDK for building AI agents with memory abstractions. Supports vector DB connectors (Azure AI Search, Chroma, Pinecone, etc.). Python, .NET, and Java SDKs. 27.3k stars. No native TypeScript SDK.
Key Insight: Memory abstraction layer with multiple vector DB connectors provides good patterns for our storage abstraction, but no TypeScript support.

Title: LangChain/LangGraph Memory
Abstract/Description: Comprehensive memory modules: ConversationBufferMemory, ConversationSummaryMemory, EntityMemory, VectorStoreMemory. LangGraph adds checkpointing and state persistence. Both Python and TypeScript SDKs available (langchain npm package). Highly extensible.
Key Insight: Mature memory abstractions with TypeScript support. However, heavy framework dependency and we don't use LangChain elsewhere. Better to adopt patterns than the library itself.

Title: AWS Bedrock Agent Memory
Abstract/Description: Built-in agent memory for Amazon Bedrock. Session memory that retains conversational context across interactions (1-365 day retention). Automatic session summarization. Memory identified by memoryId. Native AWS integration with pay-per-use pricing.
Key Insight: Native AWS memory with session summarization. Simplest integration for our AWS-native stack but limited to Bedrock Agent framework — not directly usable with Claude Code SDK.

Title: AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases
Abstract/Description: Vector store-backed knowledge retrieval for Bedrock agents. Supports OpenSearch Serverless, Aurora PostgreSQL, Pinecone, Redis as vector stores. Automatic chunking, embedding, and indexing of documents. Native RAG pipeline.
Key Insight: Could be used to store consolidated learnings as documents that agents retrieve via RAG. AWS-native but adds infrastructure complexity.

Title: Amazon Titan Embeddings
Abstract/Description: Foundation model for generating text embeddings via Bedrock API. Supports 1024-dimension vectors. Pay-per-token pricing. Available in us-east-1. Can be called directly from TypeScript via AWS SDK.
Key Insight: Direct embedding generation from our TypeScript agent via AWS SDK. No additional infrastructure needed. Essential for vector-based memory retrieval.

Title: Amazon DynamoDB
Abstract/Description: Fully managed NoSQL database. Single-digit millisecond latency. Supports TTL for automatic expiry. GSIs for flexible queries. Pay-per-request pricing. Native TypeScript SDK (@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb). Already used in our infrastructure.
Key Insight: Already in our stack, supports TTL for memory expiry, GSIs for domain-based queries. Ideal primary store for structured memory records.

Title: Amazon S3
Abstract/Description: Object storage for any volume. Already used in our infrastructure. Can store raw learning files, embeddings, and archived memories. Versioning for memory evolution tracking.
Key Insight: Already in our stack. Ideal for archival memory storage and raw learning file backup. Combine with DynamoDB for hot/cold memory tiers.

Title: Pinecone
Abstract/Description: Purpose-built vector database as a service. Serverless option with pay-per-query pricing. Sub-100ms latency. Supports metadata filtering alongside vector search. REST API and Node.js SDK available.
Key Insight: Powerful vector search but adds external dependency. For our scale (<1K records initially), DynamoDB + application-side similarity may suffice.

Title: Zep Cloud
Abstract/Description: Commercial temporal knowledge graph platform. Automatic fact extraction and relationship tracking. Sub-200ms retrieval. TypeScript SDK available. Usage-based pricing.
Key Insight: Powerful temporal knowledge graph but adds vendor dependency. Better for high-volume chat applications than our episodic agent memory use case.

Title: Mem0 Platform
Abstract/Description: Managed memory platform. SOC 2 and GDPR compliant. Multi-level memory with automatic analysis. TypeScript SDK via npm. Free tier available.
Key Insight: Managed memory with TypeScript SDK. Could accelerate Phase 1 implementation. Risk: vendor dependency for core agent capability.

Title: Chroma
Abstract/Description: Open-source embedding database. Supports local and cloud deployment. Python and JavaScript/TypeScript clients. Simple API for add/query operations. Apache 2.0 license.
Key Insight: Simple embedding DB that could run locally or in cloud. Good for prototyping but DynamoDB with Titan Embeddings is more AWS-native for production.
